title: Sticky Penalty Tracker and Cross-Region Soft-Stall Mitigation
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: During a recent outage window we observed repeated rapid reopen cycles for tenant circuits in some regions. The root cause was a combination of transient infra flakiness and an aggressive per-tenant penalty decay which allowed a tenant to re-enter normal routing too quickly, only to trigger another short-lived failure and cause oscillation. This PR introduces a 'Sticky Penalty Tracker' that records recent circuit transition history and applies a progressively longer soft-stall (slo-relaxation window) for tenants that show repeated failures within a short time window. The feature is intentionally non-blocking: it surfaces a soft-stall that influences routing and request admission but keeps logs, metrics, and an override path for emergency rollback.

What this changes (summary): - New in-memory StickyPenaltyTracker component used by the routing and SLO enforcer to compute an additional soft-stall multiplier for tenants with repeated circuit flips. - Cross-region coordinator shim (best-effort pubsub via region heartbeat channel) so adjacent regions can avoid immediate failover loops by learning about sticky penalties without requiring strong consistency. - Backward-compatible API flags: feature gate redwood.runtime.sticky_penalty.enabled (off by default for canary), and redwood.sre.stall_override for emergency bypass. - Telemetry: new histograms and tags (sticky_penalty.age_buckets, sticky_penalty.count) plus event logs for penalty application. - Tests: unit tests for penalty decay math, integration tests simulating flip cycles, and a small perf bench to validate negligible added p99 latency.

Design details: - Penalty calculation is time-decayed exponential: penalty = base * (1 + alpha)^{n_recent} clipped to max_penalty; n_recent counts flips in sliding window. Decay half-life is configurable per-tenant. - StickyTracker persists minimal state in the existing tenant metadata store (one small protobuf record per tenant) with tombstoning to avoid metadata churn; on Private installs this is optional and defaults to in-memory only. - Cross-region exposure is publish-only: regions emit short-lived announcements (tenant id + penalty snapshot) to the heartbeat channel; recipients treat these as advisory. This prevents aggressive cross-region failover when one region is oscillating.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated and disabled by default. - Step 1: Enable in internal canary (hosted internal cluster) for 48h, observe penalty histograms and failure-rate correlation. - Step 2: Enable for 10% of production tenants (weighted by traffic) and monitor p95/p99 latency, SLO violations, and failover events. - Step 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with staged decay tuning. The PR includes a runbook section for emergency disable (flip redwood.runtime.sticky_penalty.enabled=false) and a fast override via redwood.sre.stall_override.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests cover decay math, edge cases for max clipping, and garbage collection of old entries. - Integration test harness simulates repeated short failures and shows reduced oscillation and fewer cross-region failovers. - Small perf microbenchmark shows ~0.05ms median overhead on the routing hot path and no measurable p99 change under 1000 concurrent requests in CI.

Acceptance criteria: - No increase in p99 latency in production canary over 24h. - Reduction in repeated failover count by >=40% for affected tenants in the test scenario. - CI green and security review completed.

Notes and related work: This complements earlier SLO relaxation features by adding temporal stickiness to avoid rapid reopen cycles. See linear items ENG-2481 and follow-up notes in SUP-7790. For Private installations that enable persistent tenant metadata, there is a migration note: new tiny protobuf record id=sticky_penalty_v1.

References: internal runbook link: https://linear.app/reports/ENG-2481/notes, design doc: docs/runtime/sticky-penalty-tracker.md.
